is_trade_type_variant: BTIC is a trade TYPE, but on every one of my ten shapes CME lists the BTIC instrument as a separately scheduled Globex product and publishes trading hours for it that DIFFER from the underlying's. That is sourced, not inferred: (a) CME's own New Product Summaries for the 2015 launch of EST/NQT/YMT give "Globex: Sunday- Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. New York time/ET (5:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. Chicago Time/CT)" while the outrights run to 4:00 p.m. CT; (b) CME's 2025 Equity Index Sector Futures Overview prints two hours lines side by side — outright "Sunday 6:00 p.m. - Friday - 5:00 p.m. ET ... with a daily maintenance period from 5:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. ET" and "BTIC: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET"; (c) the 2026-08-10 Japanese fact card prints "Outrights: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. ET" against "BTIC: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. ET - 3:30 p.m. Tokyo time"; (d) the FX BTIC FAQ gives 6EB the FX envelope PLUS a "Trading halt from 3:40 p.m. London time ... to 4:30 p.m. London Time" that the underlying 6E does not have; (e) the crypto BTIC FAQ gives three different Globex hour sets anchored on 4:00 p.m. London, 4:00 p.m. New York and 4:00 p.m. Hong Kong/Singapore. This is NOT a blanket rule for BTIC, and I checked the counterexample deliberately: in inventory row 3 (not my group) AW (Bloomberg Commodity Index futures) and AWT (its BTIC) fall in ONE exact signature — Ready 13:15 UTC / 08:15 CT, Close 18:30 UTC / 13:30 CT — so there a BTIC really does ride the underlying's clock. On my ten rows it does not. Separately, the repo has already decided this for itself in three places: `globex_equity_index` scope is "excluding full-size `SP`, NKD, BTIC, and TACO", `globex_fx` excludes "eFix, BTIC, TAS, options", `globex_energy` excludes "TAS/TAM/BTIC", and `cme_nikkei.rs` calls BTIC "a separately scheduled trade-registration facility rather than a phase of the outright order book". So no BTIC root in this group may borrow an existing key. On the settlement/termination trap: I checked it. The Japanese fact card lists 3:30 p.m. Tokyo in BOTH a "TRADING HOURS" row and a separate "TERMINATION OF TRADING ... on the last trading day of the contract month" row — the hours row is what makes it a session boundary, and the LTD row is a different fact about the expiring month. The 15:00 CT equity close and the 3:40 p.m. London FX halt likewise come from rows CME labels "Trading Hours"/"CME Globex Trading Hours", not from settlement language.

ROW 34 (6EB; sig 2ef86ee889cd) -> proposed `globex_fx_btic_euro`. This is the subtlest one and the closest to the settlement trap. CME's FX BTIC FAQ gives 'BTIC on Euro FX Futures — CME Globex Trading Hours: Sunday-Friday 5:00 p.m.-4:00 p.m. CT. Trading halt from 3:40 p.m. London time (9:40 a.m./10:40 a.m. CT) to 4:30 p.m. London Time (10:30 a.m./11:30 a.m. CT). Daily maintenance period from 4:00 p.m.-5:00 p.m. CT.' So CME's own words make 6EB the STANDARD FX envelope with an extra 50-minute intraday halt — the 3:40 p.m. London instant is a halt in CME's language, and the schedule feed's status-4 at 14:40 UTC is a trade-date roll (the FAQ: trades after it 'are treated as having a T+1 trade date'), not a claim that the product's daily session ends there. It still cannot reuse `globex_fx`: that key's scope explicitly excludes BTIC, and the halt is a real non-tradable window `globex_fx` does not carry. Launch is dated: 'The first day of trading for BTIC and BTIC+ is Monday February 6, 2023.' MODELLING NOTE: the halt endpoints are anchored to Europe/London inside an America/Chicago envelope, so the CT times shift (9:40/10:40 CT) across the ~3 weeks a year the two zones' DST disagree. RELATED: 6EP (Euro FX BTIC+) is NOT in this row — the same FAQ gives it 'Sunday-Friday 5:00 p.m.-4:00 p.m. CT. Daily maintenance period from 4:00 p.m.-5:00 p.m. CT' with no halt, which is why the catalog puts 6EP in the 1,146-root row-1 envelope.
